tokyo_onigiri_asakusa_yadoroku.price_note: PARTIAL: the shop publishes its lunch sets with from-prices and does NOT publish its fillings list or the price of individual onigiri. It states 320円以上のおにぎりは差額分で承ります — onigiri above ¥320 are charged at the difference — which establishes ¥320 as the base but names no filling, so nothing is recorded about what they are. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ AN ONIGIRI SPECIALIST IS ONE OF THE BEST FORMATS IN JAPAN FOR A COELIAC AND THIS IS THE OLDEST ONE IN TOKYO, opened 昭和29年 (1954). The construction is rice, nori and a filling: no batter, no noodle, no wrapper, no fryer, no roux. The shop names its own components — 大釜で炊かれたコシヒカリ, Koshihikari rice cooked in a large cauldron, wrapped in 江戸前の海苔, Edo-mae nori — and rice and seaweed are both clean. ⚠ SO THE WHOLE QUESTION IS THE FILLING, AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. The standard Japanese onigiri fillings divide sharply: 梅 (pickled plum) and 塩 are clean and plant; 昆布 is kelp simmered in SOY; おかか is bonito flakes with SOY, so fish and wheat; 鮭 and 明太子 and ツナマヨ are fish, the last with egg. A coeliac or vegan here has a real meal available and has to ask filling by filling — which at a counter that hands-forms one at a time, as this shop says it does (1個から握ります), is a conversation the format actually allows. ⚠ AND THE SET HAS TWO OTHER COMPONENTS: both lunch sets come with 豆腐味噌汁 and 沢庵. The miso soup is built on a DASHI, so it is fish and the miso may be barley; the takuan is pickled daikon, plant, though commercial takuan is often steeped in a soy-bearing liquid. 台東区浅草3-9-10, behind the Sensoji main hall; 11:30 and 17:00 seatings, closing when the rice runs out; closed Sundays at lunch and Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday evenings; 8 counter seats and 8 at tables. Takeaway available and the shop delivers across Asakusa for large orders.

The MISO SOUP is the reason both flags are against rather than open: a Japanese miso soup is built on bonito DASHI, which makes the set fish, and miso koji is sometimes barley. Ask whether the soup can be left off or made without dashi, and the rest of this plate becomes one of the better prospects in Asakusa.

tokyo_karaage_yukari_asakusa_s.price_note: ⚠ CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD. It previously said the shop’s アレルゲン一覧 could not be read — that 2,281 characters of row numbers came out and not one dish name. That was WRONG, and the cause was tooling, not the PDF. Poppler on this machine carries no Adobe-Japan1 CID data, so pdftotext silently drops every Japanese glyph and returns only the ASCII, which is indistinguishable from an image-only scan. PyMuPDF decodes it completely, and reading the grid positionally (word coordinates, not reading order) is the only way to keep each ● attached to its own column, because the marks and the vertical column headers are separate text runs. The table below is now sourced from the shop’s own sheet dated 2026-05-22. The same correction applies to 俺の割烹 and RAKERU; ニューヨーカーズカフェ and 権八 really are image scans. ⚠ THE SHEET USES THREE MARKS AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE VALUE: ○ = used as an ingredient. ☆ = 店舗にて、調理器具を共有 — shared cooking equipment in the shop. △ = shared production line at the factory. Almost nothing in this dataset separates ingredient from cross-contact; this does, per dish, across all 28 designated and quasi-designated allergens, traced 原材料までさかのぼり. ⚠ TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE WHAT THIS RECORD SAYS. First: every kara-age carries ○さば — MACKEREL, as an ingredient, in a fried chicken shop. Nothing on the menu names fish; it is in the marinade, and a fish-allergic or vegetarian diner reading the board would never see it. Second: 皮せん and ポテトフライ carry 小麦 as ☆, not ○ — no wheat in the item, wheat on the shared equipment — which is exactly what the earlier version of this record guessed and is now confirmed rather than assumed. ⚠ AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: ご飯 AND ご飯(大盛) ARE MARKED ☆ ACROSS THE BOARD — wheat, egg, dairy, chicken, soy, mackerel, apple and sesame, all as shared-equipment marks. Plain rice, the thing a coeliac orders when everything else is fried, is not clean here. The shop’s own caveats: cross-contact is possible via utensils despite care, sensitivity varies by individual so judge with a specialist, the menu changes and the sheet is updated with it, and some branches do not carry every item.

Chicken skin crisps without a coating, so there is no flour in the item — and it comes out of the karaage fryer, so it is still flagged against. さば is ☆ here too rather than ○. This is what the distinction between ○ and ☆ is for.

⚠ EVERY ALLERGEN ON THIS ROW IS ☆, NOT ○ — wheat, egg, dairy, chicken, soy, mackerel, apple and sesame are all shared-equipment marks. So the chips contain none of them and touch all of them. Potato and oil, in the karaage fryer. The cheapest item on the menu.

⚠ THE ONLY BENTO WHERE 乳 AND 卵 ARE BOTH ○ — dairy and egg as ingredients, which is the TARTARE. Plus ○小麦 in the coating and the sweet-vinegar soy sauce, and ○リンゴ, apple, which is in that sauce and appears nowhere in the dish name. The most expensive bento.
A limited フェア item, listed on the allergen sheet without a price on the menu page, so the price field is left empty. ○小麦 ○鶏肉 ○大豆 ○さば — the 出汁 in the name is why さば runs through this whole board.

⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THE SHEET. Plain steamed rice is marked ☆ for 小麦, 乳, 卵, 鶏肉, 大豆, さば, リンゴ and ごま — shared equipment on all of them. Rice is the thing a coeliac reaches for when the rest of the menu is fried, and at this shop it is not a clean plate: it is served in a kitchen whose utensils carry wheat. No price is published on the menu page.
The same ☆ marks as the regular rice.

tokyo_piemon.price_note: The shop publishes its full lunch card with prices, tax included (※価格は税込みです), and portions are stated up front: 並盛り280g, 大盛り380g +150円, 特盛り480g +200円 — a 280 g base portion is already large and the shop jokes that the real quantity exceeds the printed number. Open since 昭和55年 (1980) in a converted 古民家 at Kudanshita; lunch 11:00-17:30, no lunch reservations taken. Dinner adds pizza and tapas and was not read for this record. ⚠ THIS IS A DEDICATED BOILED-PASTA HOUSE AND THE COELIAC ANSWER IS NO ACROSS THE ENTIRE FOOD MENU — every one of the fifty pasta plates is durum wheat, and the shop's own pitch is 南イタリアの極上の低温乾燥パスタ, imported dried pasta. There is no rice dish, no gluten-free noodle and no non-pasta main. What is worth recording is WHY the list is fifty items long, because it is not fifty sauces: it is one Japanese butter-and-soy idiom, 和風バター, permuted across tarako, mentaiko, natto, squid, uni, tuna and ume-shiso in every combination. ⚠ AND THAT IDIOM IS A DOUBLE TRAP RATHER THAN A SINGLE ONE. 和風バター means butter, so the whole 32-item block is out for a vegan as well as a coeliac, and the 和風 part conventionally means soy sauce or 醤油 seasoning on top of the wheat noodle — two independent wheat routes in one plate. たらこ and 明太子 are salted pollock roe, cured in blends that routinely include soy and mirin, so they are not a way around it either. ⚠ THE NEAREST THING TO A SAFE ORDER IS IN 野菜もんて AND ドルチェもんて, and even there it is thin: the salads are the only non-pasta savoury items, but 木の実とパプリカのシーザーサラダ is a caesar (anchovy, egg, parmesan, and croutons unless refused) and ジャコとバリバリ大根 is dressed with a Japanese dressing that is not described. The dessert アフォガート at 490円 is espresso over ice cream — dairy, but the only plate on the card with no wheat in its definition. Drinks are a flat 430円 and コーヒー, 紅茶 and the juices are the genuinely clean lines.

tokyo_wine_bistro_tommy_grill.price_note: PARTIAL BECAUSE THE SHOP SAYS SO TWICE: the à la carte page carries 「※仕入れによってメニューが変わりますのでご了承ください」 and repeats it under the tapas block — the card rotates with what the kitchen buys, and the dishes below are the ones printed as of this check. Prices are 全て税込み, tax included, which the page states explicitly. A Suidobashi wine bistro with counter seating, an owner who is a sommelier, and produce bought direct from contract farms in Kagoshima, Niigata and Kawagoe with fish from Chiba ports or Tsukiji middlemen; the page notes almost every à la carte plate is served with six or seven vegetables. The wine list and the course menu are on separate pages that were not read for this record. ⚠ THE USEFUL FINDING HERE IS THAT A FRENCH-JAPANESE BISTRO SPLITS CLEANLY DOWN THE MIDDLE, AND THE LINE IS THE DEMI-GLACE. Everything under 洋食屋のお食事メニュー and メインディッシュ that names デミグラス is a flat no: demi-glace is built on a brown roux, i.e. flour cooked in fat, and it is on the beef curry and the hamburg steak. The タンシチュー is the same sauce family. ⚠ WHAT SITS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THAT LINE IS GENUINELY WORTH THE TRIP, WHICH IS RARE. The four ALL 580円 tapas are cold preparations — a champagne-vinegar marinade of scallop and octopus, a chicken-and-fig terrine, an escabeche, a pork-and-walnut pâté — and escabeche and vinegar marinades contain no wheat by definition. Same for the カルパッチョ at 980円 and the 安納芋のエスカベッシュ at 580円. All are recorded ask rather than gf, because the shop publishes no allergen sheet and terrines and pâtés are frequently bound or served with bread — but this is a kitchen whose best dishes happen to be the ones without flour in them. ⚠ TWO SPECIFIC WARNINGS. The エビのアヒージョ at 1,280円 is itself just prawn, broccoli and oil, and the shop tells you to mop the oil up ぜひバゲットと合わせて — the baguette is the wheat, and it can simply be declined. And the ナポリタンパスタ at 1,180円 is wheat pasta whatever the season. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THIS IS A HARD ROOM: every single printed dish contains meat, fish, dairy or egg, and the salads are anchovy-caesar and a leaf salad with an undescribed dressing. The 有機サニーレタスとグリーンリーフのサラダ at 880円 with its stated トマトと玉ねぎのドレッシング is the only plate that might come out plant-only, and it needs asking.

tokyo_anko_maruyamacho_ten.price_note: EMPTY, AND FOR THE CLEANEST POSSIBLE REASON: THE SHOP'S OWN SITE HAS A MENU SECTION WHOSE ENTIRE CONTENT IS A POINTER SOMEWHERE ELSE. Under the heading 'Menu', grill-anko.jp/maruyamacho/ prints one sentence — 「最新のメニューは「食べログ庵狐円山町店」をご覧ください」 — and links out. There is no dish list, no price, no PDF and no image board anywhere on the page; the rest of it is the address block, a recruitment link, an August 2025 notice about changed opening hours, and the group's other shops (魚潮 学芸大学, 海と 高田馬場, まさら, Rollup Burrito). ⚠ THAT PUTS THIS RECORD IN THE ONE CATEGORY THIS TICK CANNOT FINISH: the first-party site is reachable and deliberately defers to Tabelog, and Tabelog has served this egress a Cloudflare managed challenge (HTTP 403) since 2026-09-02. It is not that the menu does not exist — it is that the only publisher of it is the blocked host. Recorded empty so the queue stops re-selecting it; it should be revisited the day Tabelog is reachable again. What the page does establish: 庵狐 円山町店, 渋谷区円山町25-4 加藤ビル1F, tel 03-5459-4083, 18:00 (Mon–Fri) / 17:00 (Sat, Sun, holidays) to 24:00 with last orders at 23:00, open year-round, 34 seats with one private room.

tokyo_tsukesoba_kanda_katsumot.price_note: The 勝本 group publishes this shop's whole board in English on its own site with a tax-included price on every line, so the figures below need no conversion or inference. 東京都千代田区神田猿楽町1-2-4 猿楽町ビル, 10:00–17:00 and closed as soon as the soup runs out, shut every Sunday with irregular Monday closures. The shop's own description of the bowl: a clear soup concentrated from fresh niboshi (dried sardines) from Kujukushima in Nagasaki, lifted with yuzu, and finished at the end of the meal with a Japanese dashi soup and a squeeze of sudachi. ⚠ THE ONE FACT A COELIAC NEEDS IS IN THE SHOP'S OWN SELLING POINT AND IT IS EASY TO MISREAD AS GOOD NEWS. Katsumoto's headline is that every bowl carries TWO kinds of noodle at once — a chewy thin noodle and a smooth flat noodle, both made for it by 浅草開化楼 — and both of them are wheat. A tsukesoba shop that doubles the noodle doubles the gluten; there is no rice or non-noodle route through this menu at all, and the menu is four bowls, five toppings, beer and a frozen souvenir pack. ⚠ AND THE NAME IS THE OTHER TRAP: 'そば' here does not mean buckwheat. つけそば in a ramen context means a wheat ramen noodle served for dipping, and the dipping sauce is 醤油 — the menu says so in English on every line, 'soy sauce dipping noodles'. Soy sauce is wheat, so the broth and the noodle fail on the same grain. ⚠ NOTHING ON THIS BOARD IS VEGAN EITHER: the soup is a sardine dashi from the first line of the shop's own description, and the toppings are egg and pork.

tokyo_sumibi_kushiyaki_hiyoku_.price_note: THE MENU EXISTS, IS BRANCH-SPECIFIC, AND IS UNREADABLE AS TEXT — THAT IS THE FINDING, AND IT IS A RECOVERABLE ONE. 炭火串焼ヒヨク之トリ publishes a real 水道橋店 menu page at /suidobashi/suidobashi_menu.html with three sections — FOOD MENU, DRINK MENU and WINE LIST — but every one of them is a flat JPEG. The page contains no prices, no item names and no PDF in its markup; there is nothing to quote. The five images are named for this branch and dated, so a future pass that can read pictures should go straight to them: _src/8114/202604_menu_suidobashi-1.jpg, _src/8108/202604_menu_suidobashi-2.jpg, _src/8112/202604_menu_suidobashi-3.jpg, _src/8116/202604_menu_suidobashi-4.jpg, and _src/4193/202104wine.jpg — all relative to https://www.hiyokuno-tori.com/. The 2026-04 date on four of the five says the card is current. This is recorded as an empty rather than a failure because the harvest is complete for a text tool; it is NOT an honest empty in the sense of "the shop publishes nothing", and it should be re-opened by an image-capable pass rather than left alone. ⚠ 焼鳥/串焼き IS A TARE KITCHEN. Yakitori is either 塩 or タレ, and the tare is a soy-sauce-and-mirin glaze that is brushed on at the grill and kept in a communal dipping pot — so even a salt-ordered skewer shares the charcoal and the tongs. Expect no allergen sheet.

tokyo_jidori_to_shochu_torichu.price_note: 地鶏と焼酎 とりちゅう (千代田区三崎町2-13-6, Suidōbashi) publishes its whole card — food, a 30-plus-label shochu list and drinks — on its own Gnavi shop site. The house does one thing: it buys 知覧鶏 from Kagoshima a whole bird at a time and serves it raw as tataki, black-seared, or skewered, and it pours the shochu of the same prefecture. ⚠ THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS THE SHOCHU SHELF, and it is also the trap. Sweet-potato shochu is distilled, so the spirit itself carries no gluten protein, but Japanese 芋焼酎 is made with a rice or BARLEY koji that the label rarely names, and the shop's own list includes two explicitly barley entries — 麦冠情け嶋 and, on the bottle list, the same again — plus a 米焼酎 (武者返し) and a 黒糖 (朝日, 長雲). A coeliac who wants certainty should take a 米焼酎 or a 黒糖焼酎 and ask about the koji; every 芋 below is recorded as ask for exactly that reason. The 本日の麦焼酎ハイボール is barley and is recorded as no. ⚠ On the food, the two 焼きおにぎり are rice but are glazed with miso or soy before grilling, the 出汁醤油のTKG is a house soy, and 梅水晶 and the pickles are soy- or dashi-cured. The 温かい湯豆腐 is offered 「お好みでお塩かポン酢で」— salt OR ponzu — which is the one dish on this menu where a coeliac has a real choice to make at the table.
